chunks: Woe to me! Would that I had not taken so-and-so as a friend!
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about regretting bad friendships in the afterlife?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Al-Furqan is often interpreted as the cry of the misguided in Hell, specifically regretting their alliance with Shaytan or false leaders who misled them. It underscores the ethical principle of *wilayah* (spiritual authority) and *shirk* (associating partners with God), where choosing a 'khalil' (intimate friend) who leads away from divine truth results in eternal separation. The regret highlights the irreversible consequence of prioritizing worldly alliances over spiritual guidance.
